title: Service accounts are workload identities
summary: A service account represents an application or workload. It is different from a person's user account.
introduction: A service account represents an application or workload. It is different from a person's user account. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain service accounts are workload identities
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A service account represents an application or workload. It is different from a person's user account.

blocks.code:
Workload: approved report task
Identity: its own service account
Access: only the data needed for the report
blocks.title: Service accounts are workload identities

blocks.text: A separate identity makes the workload's access easier to limit and review.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Describe what access a read-only report needs.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Avoid downloading long-lived keys when a supported keyless identity method fits the task.
For more detail later, use this [Google Cloud Platform further reading](https://cloud.google.com/docs/overview).
